absent: How virtual SMP presence is decided and how the topology register is accessed.
Internal layouts of trampoline header, real-mode header, blob sections and relocation tables.
Runtime behavior of secondary startup targets and boot descriptor tables.
Detailed contracts of default resource, firmware-table, interrupt, PCI, ACPI and clock handlers beyond hook names.
Post-publication discipline for the trampoline lock and secondary CPU coordination.
Derivation of mitigation thunk alignment and aliasing distances.
Exact reclaim timing and mechanism for initialization-only link regions.

findings.text: The linked image declares its physical entry from the 64 bit startup symbol relative to load offset on 64 bit builds, with an analogous 32 bit startup symbol on 32 bit builds.

The link orders executable text first, then read only data, then writable data, then diagnostic metadata, then a reclaimable initialization span, then persistent no-save, zero-initialized, reservation-limit, bootstrap and image-end markers, with encryption scratch outside the image when configured.

Sixty-four-bit builds use huge-page alignment for read-only and entry-text spans to preserve large mappings and isolation, middle-page alignment for decrypted zero-initialized data to avoid splits, and program headers marking text read-execute, data read-write and notes as note.

Build-time checks require empty or minimal linkage and relocation sections, bound total image size except for compile-test builds, and enforce cache-line placement and aliasing distances for return mitigations and indirect-branch thunks.
Topology register offset has value sixteen.
Virtual SMP detection state starts as negative one, denoting not yet probed.
Real-mode blob end marker has value 0x65a22c82.
Real-mode helper provides a far jump to a caller-supplied target through the real-mode segment.
Real-mode header defines its own include guard macro.

Default hooks include silent void and integer-argument operations, an IOMMU initializer reporting success, a false-returning boolean probe, and wall-clock fallbacks where setting reports invalid argument and reading does nothing.
Device-tree matching for the wall clock looks for a Motorola 146818 compatible node with an empty terminator entry.
During timer initialization the wall-clock setup looks up the CMOS node and, when a matching node exists but is marked unavailable, substitutes silent wall-clock accessors for default CMOS accessors.

Default initialization vector groups resource, firmware-table, interrupt, OEM, paging, timer, IOMMU, PCI, hypervisor and ACPI phases, with wall-clock setup delegated to device-tree aware handling and IOMMU defaulting to silent success.
Default CPU bring-up vector keeps early per-CPU clock handling silent, uses secondary APIC clock setup for later CPUs, and enables parallel bring-up.

Default platform vector provides native CPU and TSC calibration, CMOS wall-clock access, ISA range checking, silent NMI initialization with default reason fetching, TSC scheduler-clock save and restore, low-memory reservation and trampoline initialization, plus silent hypervisor pinning and encryption helpers reporting success, no flush need and no private MMIO.
Default APIC operations provide native IO APIC reading and native boot interrupt-mode restoration.
Real-mode support keeps a pointer to the trampoline header area, a pointer to the 32 bit trampoline CR4 image, and a top-level page-table entry value used for the trampoline identity mapping.

Trampoline lifetime proceeds from reservation below the configured real-mode limit with unconditional low-megabyte reservation, to copying and relocating the blob and publishing header fields, to tightening execute and read-only permissions, with initialization failing if no area was reserved and late initialization delegating through the platform vector.

Sixty-four-bit trampoline publication sanitizes the EFER image by clearing long-mode-active, targets secondary startup, snapshots CR4 features, clears flags, maps the low identity entry plus the full kernel high range, and applies host and guest encryption adjustments including an alternate no-verify entry when state encryption is present.
The application-processor trampoline lock is published through the header and starts cleared, denoting unlocked before any secondary CPU arrives.
Invoking real-mode initialization without a reserved header area terminates boot.

After relocation the whole trampoline span is marked non-executable, then the prefix up to the read-only end is marked read-only and the text subrange between its start and read-only end is marked executable.
A late initialization hook invokes the platform real-mode initializer and reports success.
Bootstrap allocator reservation includes sixty-four kibibytes of alignment slop between its base and limit.
Default real-mode limit is one megabyte.
